title: What Fortune Can Effect in Human Affairs and How to Withstand Her
coreMove: Build barriers before chance rises, then change methods when the times no longer fit your temperament.
sourcePressure: The chapter grants fortune great power but denies fatalism. Fortune is like a destructive flood where no barriers have been prepared. More specifically, success depends on matching one's method to the times: caution, haste, force, skill, patience, and impetuosity can each work or fail depending on circumstances. Ruin comes when a ruler prospered by one mode and cannot change when the times change. The plan must teach this without reproducing the source's misogynistic fortune image.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The wrong version becomes fatalism, hustle optimism, or adaptability slogan. The writer must show both parts: prepare defenses before the flood and change conduct when circumstances stop matching the old successful method.

hook: fortune as a woman or romantic conquest
counterintuition: most people think luck controls everything, but actually preparation wins
be bold because fortune favors the bold
tryThisNow: set a timer for ninety seconds and list risks
choose whether you are cautious or bold

exampleSpecs.domain: a lowland principality building spill canals during dry years before the river rises
exampleSpecs.audience: a ruler tempted to call floods acts of chance after refusing boring works
exampleSpecs.stakes: the river will still rise, but prepared canals decide whether it becomes disaster or force that passes through
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: In a dry month, the prince drives the first canal stake into cracked mud while courtiers laugh at flood work under a cloudless sky.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A canal stake stands in cracked mud under a cloudless sky.

exampleSpecs.domain: a cautious treaty prince whose slow method worked for ten years until a border revolt moves faster than letters
exampleSpecs.audience: a ruler who cannot leave the style that once made him successful
exampleSpecs.stakes: waiting for perfect messages now gives rebels time to seize the crossings
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: He sets the sealed inquiry packet aside, breaks the emergency horse token, and sends riders before the council archive can produce the usual precedent.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A sealed inquiry packet lies beside a snapped emergency horse token.

exampleSpecs.domain: an impetuous siege ruler who keeps storming gates after the enemy changes to layered traps
exampleSpecs.audience: a commander whose old boldness now fits the wrong moment
exampleSpecs.stakes: the same speed that once won cities now feeds soldiers into prepared snares
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The captain lays three broken assault ladders beside the new trap diagram and marks the moment when boldness stopped matching the times.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Broken assault ladders lie across a layered trap diagram.

exampleSpecs.domain: a trading city that prospered by patience in stable markets but faces a sudden embargo on its only salt road
exampleSpecs.audience: magistrates deciding whether patient bargaining still fits the times
exampleSpecs.stakes: waiting preserved prices in calm years; now waiting lets warehouses empty while rival ports reroute trade
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The magistrates predict another patient negotiation, then the warehouse tally board flips to empty salt rows before the envoy even leaves.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Empty salt rows appear on a warehouse tally board beside an unsent envoy letter.

exampleSpecs.domain: a frontier papal commander moving before allies finish objecting because delay would let the city harden
exampleSpecs.audience: a ruler whose bold action succeeds because the specific constellation rewards speed
exampleSpecs.stakes: Spain, Venice, and France each hesitate for different reasons, and the city is vulnerable only before plans become formal
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Before the foreign replies arrive, he folds the blank reply slots under the march drum and enters the road, forcing allies to react to motion instead of debate.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Blank reply slots sit beneath a march drum at dawn.

exampleSpecs.domain: a mountain federation whose old defense lines face artillery for the first time
exampleSpecs.audience: council captains who call the new weapon bad fortune instead of changing barriers and tactics
exampleSpecs.stakes: old walls were prudent once, but the new times require angled earthworks and mobile guns before the next campaign
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The engineer places an artillery dented wall stone on the old defense map, then draws the first angled earthwork where the straight wall used to be enough.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: An artillery-dented wall stone sits on an old defense map.

skillTargets: distinguish fatalism from preparing barriers before chance rises
apply the method-times fit test to caution, haste, patience, force, and skill
analyze why a formerly successful temperament becomes dangerous when circumstances change
evaluate whether boldness, caution, or preparation is being prescribed conditionally rather than as a universal slogan

tryThisNowSpec: Choose one ruler who was ruined after earlier success. Write the method that used to fit, the circumstance that changed, and the barrier or conduct change that should have been prepared before the crisis.
